newsitem.title: FRANCE: Portugal bridge conflict limited to land cost - SGE.
newsitem.headline: Portugal bridge conflict limited to land cost - SGE.

text.p: A conflict between Franco-British consortium Lusoponte and the Portuguese government over a bridge on the Tagus river only concerns extra costs related to land redevelopment, French construction company SGE said on Tuesday.
SGE, which is a unit of French utilities group Generale des Eaux, holds a 24.8 percent stake in the Lusoponte consortium.
Lusoponte said on Monday it was filing a complaint against the Portuguese government over the cost of land expropriation with the Paris International Commercial Court.
An SGE spokesman told Reuters the bridge contract set aside some 380 million escudos for land purchase but the real cost reached some two billion escudos.

"This conflict, which is not recent, only concerns how the Portuguese government is to take charge of costs related to the redevelopment of a natural area of salt marshes on the southern bank of the Tagus river, as agreed between the state and the European Commission," SGE said in a statement.
"This responsibility, which is certainly not on a scale likely to jeopardise the economics of the agreement, was specified in the original contract," it said.
The SGE executive said the Portuguese authorities agreed to a redevelopment of the natural area in exchange for European Commission subsidies.
Under the terms of the original agreement, the Lusoponte group bought the land for redevelopment on behalf of the state and would reclaim the cost of purchase.
The Vasco de Gama bridge is expected to be completed in January or February of 1998.
